content.text: All preferred elements are met across §§ 13.1–13.3, and Section 24.1 supplies the successor/M&A assignment path. Submitting compliant.

input.quote: 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.
input.rationale: The grant structure meets the preferred position in full. § 13.1 extends the subscription grant to "Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf" (no written-notice condition needed), and § 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a "perpetual, irrevocable" fully paid licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, including contractor support. § 13.3 limits Vendor revocation or suspension to a "material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure", satisfying the subscription-licence element, and permits transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, which under § 24.1 expressly covers a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without Vendor consent. The revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence in § 14.2 is an ownership/IP issue addressed under the IP rule and is not flagged again here; the Vendor Technology within Deliverables is in any event carried by the perpetual § 13.2 licence via § 14.3.
